title: InkEvent
description: Every event the Inkwell core sends a shell through the C ABI (core/crates/ink-ffi/include/inkwell.h): one JSON object, its kind in "type". The Swift types in mac/ are generated from this file by `cargo run -p ink-ffi --bin ink-schema`; the generator reads a subset of JSON Schema (string enums, objects of scalars, arrays and references) and refuses anything else. Optional fields are omitted, never null.

Channel.description: A side of a meeting: the mic is you, the far end is them (stream identity, architecture rule 5).

EngineSource.description: Where a routed engine comes from: registry (a model downloaded from the built-in registry) or shell (an engine the shell registered, such as FluidAudio's Parakeet on the Mac).

EngineKind.description: What kind of engine the shell registered: offline (finals), streaming (live partials) or llm (a language model, for dictation polish).

Job.description: A job the router fills with the best installed engine.

VadUnavailable.description: Why no voice detection model is in use.

Refusal.description: Why a job's model was refused.

Discard.description: Why a dictation ended without an insertion. None of these is an error.

CommandAction.description: A voice command. change_style and toggle_polish are already applied by the core; the rest are the shell's to carry out.

Risk.description: How much confirmation a voice command needs: safe runs at once, moderate gets a brief notice the user can cancel, dangerous asks first.

InsertOutcome.description: How a dictation went in. blocked: Secure Input or an elevated target refused synthetic input, and nothing was inserted. inserted_clipboard_not_restored: inserted, and the previous clipboard could not be put back.

FailedStage.description: Which stage of a dictation failed.

DictationWarning.description: Something went wrong during a dictation, and it went on without it. deleted_text_not_scrubbed and deleted_text_scrubbed: as for meetings.

SideState.description: What a meeting side is delivering, as the silent-channel watchdog judges it: ok, stopped (no audio where it must keep coming), zeros (only exact zeros: no data at all, most often a denied capture).

Phase.description: Which part of a meeting a problem came from.

MeetingWarning.description: Something went wrong in a meeting, and it went on without it. deleted_text_not_scrubbed: text the library deleted or replaced could not yet be cleared from its files (another process is reading the database; the change is saved, and the store keeps trying); deleted_text_scrubbed: it now is. Each is sent once per change. not_crash_protected: the crash-recovery marker could not be written when the meeting started, so if the app quits unexpectedly this meeting is not finished at the next launch (its audio is still saved).

KeptLive.description: Why the final pass did not replace the live transcript: refused (the supersede guard: an empty result, or a side under half its live words) or incomplete (some regions failed).

JobScore.description: An engine's measured word error rate on one job.

ChannelPass.description: What a meeting's final pass did on one side.

chunks_written.description: Chunk files the pump wrote for this side; absent when the pump did not report.

chunks.description: Chunk files the final pass found.

captured_ms.description: Audio in the readable chunks, ms. Zero: nothing was captured.

backlogged_finals.description: Live finals saved without the speech check.

audible_ms.description: Time above the audible floor, ms, before any gain.

regions.description: Speech regions the engine was given.

empty_regions.description: Regions that came back without words.

speech_ms.description: Time the VAD found as speech, ms.

CoreReady.description: The core started. The first event after ink_init.

abi.description: The core's ABI version; must equal INK_ABI_VERSION in inkwell.h.

CoreStopped.description: The last event before ink_shutdown returns.

CommandFailed.description: A command was read and could not be carried out.

id.description: The command's "id", when it had one.

message.description: Why. Names what failed, never what was said.

EngineRegistered.description: An engine the shell registered is in use: an offline or streaming engine in the router, or a language model for polish.

kind.description: What kind of engine it is.

jobs.description: The jobs it fills; empty for a language model.

items.description: A job and its error rate.

EngineRouted.description: What serves a job now, in answer to engine.route: the router's choice among installed models and registered engines. Without id, nothing installed or registered fills the job.

id.description: The engine that serves it: a registry model's id, or the id a shell engine registered under.

EngineUnregistered.description: An engine the shell registered was let go; its release function runs once no call is in flight.

ModelWarmed.description: A job's model is loaded and kept loaded.

ModelWarmFailed.description: A job's model could not be warmed.

id.description: The model's id, when one was chosen.

ModelRefused.description: A job asked for a model that is held exclusively (being updated), and was refused. The job fails; nothing was loaded from files being replaced.

ModelUpdateStarted.description: A model update holds its model: jobs that need it are refused until model.update_finished.

ModelUpdateFinished.description: A model update ended, and its hold is released.

id.description: The model that was to be replaced.

ok.description: Whether the new model is installed (and warm, if the old one was).

no_model_warm.description: The update left no model warm: dictation has no model until one is warmed.

message.description: Why it failed, when it did.

AudioDropped.description: The pump dropped capture blocks because a chain's queue was full (the chain fell behind). Sent once per stretch, when the queue takes audio again or closes.

channel.description: The side, for dictation (the mic). Absent for a meeting, whose two sides share one queue.

DictationVoiceDetection.description: Whether dictations are levelled with voice detection. Sent at the start and whenever it changes; while unavailable the shell shows it.

available.description: Whether a VAD is in use.

DictationStarted.description: A hold passed the minimum and is now a take: show that it is listening.

DictationShortPressIgnored.description: A press shorter than the minimum hold (a modifier used in a shortcut). Nothing was shown or transcribed.

DictationStopped.description: The take is closed and being processed.

DictationDiscarded.description: The take ended without an insertion.

reason.description: Why. speech_too_short: tell the user it was too short and to try again.

live_ms.description: How long the key was held, for too_short.

DictationCommand.description: The take was a voice command.

value.description: Its argument: a style, a model id, a URL, an app path, or fixed text.

DictationInserted.description: A dictation went out. Carries the user's words: never log it.

record.description: Its library record, unless saving failed.

DictationFailed.description: A take failed. Nothing was inserted for a transcription failure.

DictationWarningEvent.description: Something went wrong during a take, and it went on without it.

message.description: The error, where there was one.

DictationHotkeyLost.description: The OS removed the hotkey. Nothing more arrives until it is started again.

DictationWorkerFailed.description: A stage of the dictation chain panicked; the take in progress is lost. With recovered, the next take works. Without it the worker has stopped after repeated failures: the shell MUST unbind the dictation hotkey (unbind_hotkey is then true) and show that dictation is off, since key presses now reach nothing.

recovered.description: Whether the worker is still serving.

unbind_hotkey.description: The shell must unbind the hotkey now: always the opposite of recovered.

MeetingStarted.description: A meeting's record exists and its capture is being transcribed live. Names what the shell shows of it: its title, its app and its mic, when known.

title.description: Its title, when known at the start (a calendar event, a replay's name); otherwise the summary's headline names it later.

app.description: The app it records, by id (a bundle id on the Mac), when it was started for one.

app_name.description: That app's name, as the shell shows it.

mic_name.description: The microphone it records, as the OS names it.

MeetingDetected.description: An app has held the microphone long enough to be a call, and no meeting is being recorded: the shell offers to record it (the consent Drop), and records only if the user says so (meeting.start with this app).

app.description: The app, by id (a bundle id on the Mac).

app_name.description: Its name, as the shell shows it.

MeetingDetectionEnded.description: The offer to record an app is over before it was taken: the app released the microphone, or the user said not this one (meeting.dismiss).

dismissed.description: Whether the user dismissed it (rather than the app releasing the microphone).

MeetingDetection.description: Whether the core is listening for calls now: sent once at start whatever the state (off included, with a message when the setting could not be read), then when detection starts, stops (the meetings.detect setting), fails to start, or stops on its own (the platform stopped answering). The shell shows this state, not the setting.

listening.description: Whether apps taking the microphone are being watched.

message.description: Why not, when detection could not start or stopped on its own. Never content.

MeetingAnswered.description: An answer to meeting.ask about the live meeting: the model's words. Render them as text only (no links): model text can say anything. A failure is command.failed with the command's id. Never log it.

ref.description: The id of the meeting.ask command this answers.

MeetingRecovered.description: A meeting a crash interrupted is being finished: its recorded audio was repaired and its final pass follows (its events, ending in meeting.finished or meeting.failed).

trimmed.description: Torn partial frames cut from a chunk's end.

unrecoverable.description: Chunk files left as they were: nothing could place them.

recorded_ms.description: How much audio the meeting recorded before the crash, ms.

meetings.description: Interrupted meetings it finished or tried to.

message.description: Present when the meetings could not even be looked for (the data directory could not be listed): an interrupted meeting may be waiting, and the next launch looks again. Names what failed, never a meeting's words.

MicTransport.description: How a microphone connects: built in, Bluetooth (call-quality audio, and zeros while its user is silent), USB, a virtual or aggregate device, or anything else.

MicReason.description: Why a meeting records this microphone: the system default input; the built-in mic because the output is Bluetooth (a headset mic is call-quality audio); the headset's own mic because the user's setting says so; the default because this Mac has no built-in mic; the first input because no default is set; it was named; or a reason this build of the core does not name (unknown).

MeetingVoiceDetection.description: Whether a side is levelled with voice detection. Sent per side at the start and when it changes.

available.description: Whether a VAD is in use.

MeetingSideState.description: What a side is delivering, when that changes.

MeetingPartial.description: Provisional live text; each replaces the last and none is saved. Carries the meeting's words: never log it.

MeetingFinal.description: Settled live text, saved as revision 1. Carries the meeting's words: never log it.

MeetingWarningEvent.description: Something went wrong in a meeting, and it went on without it. Which fields are present depends on kind.

start_ms.description: Start of the stretch, ms into the meeting.

quiet_ms.description: How long the far end was without signal, ms.

audible_ms.description: Time above the audible floor, ms; for echo_path_not_found, while the far end played.

chunks.description: Chunk files skipped or cut short.

message.description: The error, where there was one. Never the meeting's words.

MeetingStopped.description: Capture ended and the record is marked ended; the final pass runs next.

MeetingTranscribed.description: The final pass finished one side.

MeetingDiarized.description: Diarization of the far end finished.

substantial.description: Clusters holding at least 2 % of the far end's speech.

labelled.description: Whether the labels were kept: at least two substantial clusters.

EchoState.description: Whether the live mic is protected from the far end's echo. searching: no echo path yet, the mic reaches the live transcript as captured (unprotected; with earbuds there is none to find); cancelling: a path was found, the live you transcript hears the cancelled mic behind the echo gate; degraded: cancelling, but the linear stage takes almost no echo off; failed: cancellation stopped, and the search starts again; found_at_end: at the end, the search that was still running found a path, so the mic went unprotected throughout it.

EchoSearch.description: Why the live echo search (re)started: the meeting started, the capture's device changed (a new device is a new echo path), or cancellation failed.

EchoFailure.description: Why echo cancellation stopped: backlog (one side ran more than 10 s ahead of the other; channel says which), bad_alignment (a path no canceller follows), stalled (the canceller gave no answer in time; it is left behind), internal (a bug inside the core, reported rather than hidden).

MeetingEcho.description: Whether the live mic is protected from echo, when it changes. Which fields are present depends on state.

why.description: Why the search began, for searching.

since_ms.description: Where the search began, ms into the meeting, for searching.

from_ms.description: Where cancellation began, ms into the meeting, for cancelling.

unprotected_ms.description: How long the mic went uncancelled since the search began, ms, for cancelling (0 when cancellation carries on along a better fit) and found_at_end.

stable_from_ms.description: Where the search's windows first supported the path, ms into the meeting, for cancelling and found_at_end.

delay_ms.description: How late the mic hears the far end, ms, for cancelling.

drift_ppm.description: How fast the mic's clock runs against the far end's, ppm, for cancelling.

erle_db.description: The linear stage's echo return loss enhancement over the last 20 s of far-end audio, dB, for degraded.

channel.description: The side that ran ahead, for a backlog.

EchoPath.description: The echo path the final pass fitted over the whole recording.

delay_ms.description: How late the mic hears the far end at the start, ms.

drift_ppm.description: How fast the mic's clock runs against the far end's, ppm.

stable_from_ms.description: Where the windows first supported it, ms into the meeting.

MeetingEchoPass.description: What echo cancellation did in the final pass. Sent before the supersede.

path.description: The path, when the recording has one.

candidates.description: Windows loud and clear enough to vote.

cancelled.description: Whether the mic was cancelled (false: no path, or cancellation failed).

erle_first_db.description: Echo return loss enhancement over the first 10 s of far-end audio, dB.

erle_db.description: Echo return loss enhancement over far-end audio after that, dB.

linear_erle_db.description: The same for the linear output alone (what the you transcript hears), dB.

removed.description: You lines removed as echo of the far end.

kept_near_speech.description: Lines that repeated the far end but were kept: the near end was heard over them.

kept_no_evidence.description: Lines that repeated the far end but were kept for want of acoustic evidence.

live_echo_finals.description: Live you finals the pass judged to be echo; the supersede guard does not count them.

start_ms.description: Its start, ms into the meeting.

RemovedEchoLine.description: A you line the final pass removed as echo of the far end. Its words are not here: the store keeps the line with the record, at index in its removed lines (by start time), so it can be put back.

index.description: Its place in the record's removed lines.

start_ms.description: Its start, ms into the meeting.

far.description: The far-end lines whose words it matched, in time order.

matched.description: How many of them matched the far end, in order.

MeetingRemovedAsEcho.description: You lines the final pass removed as echo, by place and span only. Sent only when there are some, before the supersede.

MeetingSuperseded.description: The final pass replaced the live transcript.

MeetingKeptLive.description: The final pass did not replace the live transcript, which stays as it was.

unverified.description: Items dropped because their citation did not check out.

MeetingLooksDone.description: In this meeting the user said work was already done that earlier meetings' open commitments promise: each such commitment now carries a "looks done" suggestion (commitments.list shows it) for the user to confirm or dismiss. Sent only when there is at least one.

MeetingFinished.description: Everything is done: the record is complete.

revision.description: The transcript's revision now; absent only when the live one was kept and the record could not be read.

MeetingFailed.description: A meeting could not start, or its final pass stopped before replacing the live transcript (which then stands, and the pass can run again).

record.description: The meeting's record, when it had one.

MeetingCaptureFailed.description: Capture stopped because the core's pump failed (a bug in the core, contained). What reached disk is kept: the meeting ends as if capture had stopped, and its final pass runs over it.

record.description: The meeting's record, when it had one.

MeetingWorkerFailed.description: The meeting's worker panicked and stopped. Its recorded audio is on disk; the live transcript so far is saved.

PermissionState.description: A permission's state, as the platform's probe reads it without prompting.

PermissionName.description: A permission the app depends on.

ModeStyle.description: How a mode writes: a style this build knows, or other.

OwedItem.description: An open commitment: not done, and not merged into another.

record.description: The record it was said in.

record_title.description: That record's title, when it has one.

record_started_at_unix_ms.description: When that record started, Unix ms.

recipient.description: Who it is owed to, as said, when the transcript says.

due_at_unix_ms.description: When, resolved to a time, Unix ms: what overdue is measured against.

said_at_ms.description: Where in the record it was first said, ms.

merged.description: How many other commitments were merged into it as the same promise said again.

looks_done.description: Where a later meeting suggests it is already done, until the user answers.

DoneEvidence.description: Where a later meeting suggests an open commitment is already done: the user said, there, that they had finished it. A suggestion for the user to confirm (commitment.set_done) or dismiss (commitment.not_yet).

record.description: The record it was said in.

record_title.description: That record's title, when it has one.

record_started_at_unix_ms.description: When that record started, Unix ms.

text.description: The line said there, when it is still in the record's transcript. The library's words: never log it.

ModeInfo.description: A mode: how dictation writes in the apps it names.

name.description: Its name, as the user sees and says it.

polish.description: Whether its dictations are polished (when a language model can).

remove_fillers.description: Whether fillers and stutters are removed.

apps.description: The apps it is picked for, matched against the frontmost app's identity. Never shown to the user as they are: a shell names each app.

items.description: An app identity, or part of one: on macOS a bundle id such as com.example.mail.

PermissionsChecked.description: Every permission's state now, in answer to permissions.check. Never prompts. System audio reads not_determined until the app has asked for it, because checking it before would make macOS prompt.

system_audio.description: Recording other apps' sound (the far end), verified by listening for the app's own tone.

accessibility.description: Typing into other apps, reading the focused app and the dictation key. Never asked reads as denied.

input_monitoring.description: A listen-only key tap, which the Mac app does not use. Never asked reads as denied.

PermissionRequested.description: permission.request showed the system prompt or opened the settings pane. The answer comes later: check again when the user comes back.

CommitmentsListed.description: The open commitments across the library, in answer to commitments.list: the soonest resolved due time first, undated ones last. Carries the promises' words.

CommitmentUpdated.description: A commitment was marked done or open again (commitment.set_done), or its looks-done suggestion was dismissed (commitment.not_yet). Either way, a suggestion on it is settled.

NoteAdded.description: A note was saved to a record, in answer to note.add. Its words stay with the shell that sent them.

at_ms.description: Where in the record it was written, ms.

ref.description: The command's "id", when it had one, so the shell can match the note to what it sent.
The command's "id", when it had one, so the shell can match the answer to the line that sent it.
The command's "id", when it had one, so the shell can match the answer to the line that sent it.

ModelsListed.description: The catalogue's models for this OS, in answer to models.list. What serves each job now is engine.route's answer.

models.description: The models, in the catalogue's order.

SettingValue.description: A shell setting's value, in answer to setting.get or setting.set.

value.description: Its value; absent when it has never been set.

ModesListed.description: The user's modes, in answer to modes.list, in the order they are matched: the first mode naming the frontmost app wins, else the default.

default_id.description: The mode used when no other matches.

CatalogueEntry.description: A model in the catalogue that runs on this OS.

installed.description: Whether its files are installed and complete.

jobs.description: The jobs it fills, each with its measured error rate.

items.description: A job and its error rate.

RecordKind.description: What produced a record: one dictation, a meeting (mic and far end), or an imported audio or video file.

AudioTimeline.description: How a record's chunks were placed on its timeline: recorded (from the start the meeting wrote beside them) or estimated (from its earliest chunk, because that start is missing: an older record, or one whose write failed). Estimated: the two sides may be out of step, and the shell says so.

RecordRow.description: A record as a list shows it.

title.description: Its title: a calendar event's, a file's name, or the summary's headline. Absent until one is known.

ended_at_unix_ms.description: When it ended, Unix ms; absent while it is live.

revision.description: The transcript revision: 1 while live, 2 once the final pass replaced it.

has_audio.description: Whether it kept audio (a meeting's chunks).

preview.description: The first words of an untitled record's transcript. Carries the user's words: never log it.

RecordSegment.description: Settled transcript on a record's timeline. Carries the user's words: never log it.

start_ms.description: Start, ms from the record's start.

end_ms.description: End, ms from the record's start.

speaker.description: The diarized far-end speaker, when labels were kept.

RecordNote.description: A note the user typed, stamped with where in the record it was written.

at_ms.description: Where in the record, ms from its start: the timestamp chip.

text.description: The note. The user's words: never log it.

RecordSummary.description: A record's summary, as stored: markdown (a headline, then sections). Shells render it; it is never shown raw.

text.description: The markdown. The library's words: never log it.

created_at_unix_ms.description: When it was written, Unix ms.

items.description: Its decisions and actions with the line each cites, in the order the text lists them (empty for a summary saved before they were kept).

SummaryItemKind.description: Whether a summary item is a decision or an action.

SummaryItemRow.description: A decision or an action in a summary, with the line it cites.

text.description: The item as the summary states it. The library's words: never log it.

span.description: Where the line it cites was said.

Span.description: A stretch of a record: where something was said.

start_ms.description: Start, ms from the record's start.

end_ms.description: End, ms from the record's start.

CommitmentRow.description: A commitment: something promised in a record.

text.description: What was promised. The library's words: never log it.

recipient.description: Who it is owed to, as said, when the transcript says.

due_at_unix_ms.description: When, resolved, Unix ms; absent when it could not be resolved.

provenance.description: Where in the record it was said.

merged_into.description: The commitment it was folded into ("said twice"), when it was.

looks_done.description: Where a later meeting suggests it is already done, until the user answers.

SpeakerName.description: A diarized speaker the user named in one record.

AudioChunk.description: One chunk file of a record's audio: raw little-endian float samples, interleaved, after a header of data_offset bytes.

start_ms.description: Where its first frame falls on the record's timeline, ms (negative: before the start).

RecordAudio.description: Where a record's audio is: its chunks per side, placed on its timeline.

chunks.description: Readable chunks, mic first then far end, each in order. Unreadable ones are left out (and logged).

left_out.description: Chunk files left out of the player: unreadable, or whose format or place on the timeline recovery could only guess. Nonzero: some of the audio cannot be played or placed, and the shell says so.

title.description: The record's title, when it has one.

started_at_unix_ms.description: When the record started, Unix ms.

start_ms.description: Where in the record the match is, ms.

snippet.description: The matching text. The library's words: never log it.

KindStats.description: What the library holds of one kind since a moment.

duration_ms.description: Their total length, ms (records still live count nothing).

LibraryRecords.description: Records, in answer to records.list: newest first (by start time, then id).

ref.description: The id of the command this answers, echoed so the shell can match the answer to its question.

kind.description: The kind asked for; absent for every kind.

more.description: Whether more records follow the last one: ask again with it as "before".

LibrarySearch.description: Full-text matches, in answer to records.search, best first.

ref.description: The id of the command this answers, echoed so the shell can match the answer to its question.

query.description: The query, as asked. The user's words: never log it.

LibraryRecord.description: One record whole, in answer to record.open. Carries the library's words: never log it.

ref.description: The id of the command this answers, echoed so the shell can match the answer to its question.

segments.description: The current revision's transcript, by start time.

summary.description: Its summary, when one was written.

commitments.description: Its commitments, in the order they were added, merged ones included.

audio.description: Its audio, when it kept some and the directory is there.

LibraryStats.description: What the library holds since a moment, in answer to library.stats, and whether recent meetings kept no far end.

ref.description: The id of the command this answers, echoed so the shell can match the answer to its question.

since_unix_ms.description: The moment asked about, Unix ms.

far_silent_meetings.description: The newest finished meetings in a row (of the last 20) that kept the user's words and none of the far end's: the sign that the other side was not heard.

far_silent_since_unix_ms.description: When the earliest of those started, Unix ms.

LibrarySwept.description: The retention setting deleted meetings and dictations older than it keeps (never imports), at launch, after a meeting, or when it changed. Their text is overwritten in the library's files, their audio removed.

failed.description: Records, or their audio, that could not be removed (each logged by what failed).

before_unix_ms.description: Records that started before this moment were due, Unix ms.
